gen-dafont-dited-fs-gambetta: Gambetta, a classic serif, reads bookish and graceful. Dited is the digital, tech-flavored one, its round letters sitting hip to hip, while Gambetta lets its stroke weight shift gently from stem to joint, though it is not meant for long paragraphs.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-old-turki: Cast-iron stature in lowercase, drawn with one compass-steady line. Edo SZ carries the cultural weight up top, and Noto Sans Old Turkic follows with chunky, tall, open-mouthed letters that stay approachable.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-noto-sans: Adventurous letters stride out, widely spaced and towering. Eight Bit Dragon swaggers with gently modulated strokes and no sharp hairlines, while Noto Sans Tirhuta handles contemporary clarity with a dominant x-height and cut-back terminals.
